findings.evidence: python3 -c: conn = connect(); insert (1,'paid',1000),(2,'refunded',500); find_orders(conn, "paid' OR status = 'refunded") -> [(1, 'paid', 1000), (2, 'refunded', 500)] (both rows returned); a second payload "x' ; DROP TABLE orders; --" -> sqlite3.ProgrammingError: You can only execute one statement at a time
findings.explanation: The parameterized query was replaced with an f-string, so `status` is interpolated straight into SQL. A caller-controlled status value can break out of the literal and inject arbitrary predicates (or additional statements). High severity.

findings.evidence: python3 -c: page(list(range(100)), 1)[0] == 20; page(list(range(100)), 2)[0] == 40; any(0 in page(items, n) for n in 1..6) -> False; items surfaced on pages 1..6 start at 20. (test_page_size only asserts len == 20, so it passes despite the bug.)
findings.explanation: start is now `number * size` instead of `(number - 1) * size`, so page 1 skips the first `size` items entirely and every page is shifted by one. The first 20 items are unreachable on any page. Tests only check the length (20), so this slipped through.

findings.evidence: python3 -W error::SyntaxWarning compile('app/orders.py') -> SyntaxError: "is not" with 'str' literal. Did you mean "!="?; runtime: rows [{'paid':1000},{'refunded':500}] -> revenue == 1500 (expected 1000); revenue([{'status': 'refunded' (built at runtime), 'amount': 500}]) -> 500 (expected 0).
findings.explanation: `o["status"] is not "refunded"` uses identity comparison for string values, which is wrong (and a SyntaxWarning/SyntaxError under `python -W error`). It happens to work for interned literals but refunds whose 'refunded' string was built at runtime (e.g. from the DB or string operations) are summed into revenue, overstating it.

findings.evidence: python3 -c: calls=[]; retry(failing_fn, 2, 0) -> None after 2 attempts; the exception is not propagated (verified swallowed: retry returned None)
findings.explanation: On the last failed attempt `retry` now returns None instead of re-raising. Failures are silently converted into a None return value, so callers can treat a hard failure as an empty result. Medium severity.

findings.evidence: Static inspection of the removed `try/finally` block in app/orders.py:export_paid.
findings.explanation: The sqlite connection is no longer closed in a `finally` block, so every call leaks a connection (and, on error, the exception path leaves it open too). Cannot be demonstrated by a runtime check here, but it is a straightforward resource leak.

findings.evidence: grep -rn 'app.util|import util' --include=*.py . -> no matches in the sandbox, so no breakage demonstrable; the diff itself renames app/util.py to app/helpers.py.
findings.explanation: app/util.py was renamed to app/helpers.py; any remaining `from app.util import money` / `import app.util` outside the diff would now ImportError. No such importer exists in this repo, so it is informational only.
